dest.ksamilDesc: Small peninsula village with turquoise water and tiny islands.
dest.ksamilTip: Visit in June or September to avoid the biggest crowds.
dest.dhermiDesc: Riviera beach village beneath the Ceraunian mountains.
dest.dhermiTip: Sunbeds fill up early in August — arrive before 10:00.
dest.palaseDesc: Long, quiet beach at the foot of the Llogara Pass.
dest.palaseTip: Great sunset views from the southern end of the beach.
dest.jaleDesc: Small lively bay popular with young travelers.
dest.jaleTip: Beach bars host events on summer weekends.
dest.blueEyeDesc: Natural spring with intense blue water, deep in the forest.
dest.blueEyeTip: Bring comfortable shoes — the walk from the parking takes a while.
dest.butrintDesc: UNESCO ancient city with Greek, Roman and Venetian ruins.
dest.butrintTip: Go early in the morning; the site has little shade.
dest.beratDesc: UNESCO “town of a thousand windows” with Ottoman houses.
dest.beratTip: Climb to the castle quarter for panoramic views.
dest.gjirokasterDesc: UNESCO stone town with a grand hilltop fortress.
dest.gjirokasterTip: Try qifqi, the local rice-ball specialty.
dest.krujeDesc: Historic castle town of the national hero Skanderbeg.
dest.krujeTip: The old bazaar is perfect for souvenirs.
dest.rozafaDesc: Legendary castle overlooking Shkodër and three rivers.
dest.rozafaTip: Visit at sunset for the best light over the lake.
dest.thethDesc: Alpine national park with waterfalls and stone towers.
dest.thethTip: The Theth–Valbona hike takes 6–8 hours; start early.
dest.valbonaDesc: Dramatic alpine valley in the Accursed Mountains.
dest.valbonaTip: Book guesthouses ahead in July and August.
dest.llogaraDesc: Mountain pass with sweeping views over the Riviera.
dest.llogaraTip: Stop at the viewpoint on the way to the beaches.
dest.dajtiDesc: Tirana’s mountain, reachable by cable car.
dest.dajtiTip: Check the cable car opening times before you go.
dest.nationalMuseumDesc: Albania’s largest museum, on Skanderbeg Square.
dest.nationalMuseumTip: Plan around two hours for the main exhibitions.
dest.bunkartDesc: Cold-War bunker turned history and art museum.
dest.bunkartTip: Bring a light jacket — it is cool underground.
dest.pazariRiDesc: Tirana’s renovated central market with local produce.
dest.pazariRiTip: Morning is the best time for fresh fruit and byrek.
dest.korcaDesc: Historic bazaar town known for serenades and local beer.
dest.korcaTip: Try the local kernacka and a Korça beer.
dest.tiranaCenterDesc: Albania’s lively capital square, ringed by museums, cafés and the National History Museum.
dest.tiranaCenterTip: Free walking tours usually start here — a good first stop in the city.
dest.durresDesc: One of the largest Roman amphitheatres in the Balkans, in the heart of Albania's main port city.
dest.durresTip: Combine with a walk along the Durrës beach promenade nearby.
dest.vloreDesc: Waterfront monument marking Albania's 1912 declaration of independence.
dest.vloreTip: Sunset over the bay here is one of the best views on the coast.
dest.himareDesc: Riviera town with a hilltop old quarter overlooking pebble beaches.
dest.himareTip: Climb to the old town in the evening for a cooler walk and sea views.
dest.pogradecDesc: Shoreline town on Lake Ohrid, one of Europe's oldest and deepest lakes.
dest.pogradecTip: Try the local koran fish, native to the lake.
dest.shkoderLakeDesc: The largest lake in Southern Europe, shared with Montenegro, near Rozafa Castle.
dest.shkoderLakeTip: Boat trips from Shirokë are a relaxed way to see the lake.
dest.divjakaDesc: Coastal national park and lagoon, home to the rare Dalmatian pelican.
dest.divjakaTip: Bring binoculars — early morning is best for birdwatching.
dest.voskopojaDesc: Historic mountain village once a major Balkan trading centre, known for frescoed churches.
dest.voskopojaTip: Several 18th-century churches are only a short walk apart.
dest.permetDesc: Riverside town in the Vjosa valley, a gateway to thermal springs and the Vjosa Wild River National Park.
dest.permetTip: Pair a Përmet visit with the Bënjë hot springs and a raki tasting — the region is known for its fruit brandy.
dest.shalaRiverDesc: Turquoise mountain river winding through steep canyon walls near Theth, reachable by boat from Koman Lake.
dest.shalaRiverTip: Combine with the Koman Lake ferry for one of the most scenic boat rides in the Balkans.
dest.osumCanyonDesc: Dramatic limestone gorge near Çorovodë, with turquoise pools carved into the rock.
dest.osumCanyonTip: Guided rafting trips run from spring through early autumn.
dest.mriziIZanaveDesc: Farm-to-table restaurant in Fishtë pioneering Albania's slow-food movement with home-grown ingredients.
dest.mriziIZanaveTip: Book ahead — the tasting menu is built around whatever the farm harvested that day.
dest.cercizIsmetShehuDesc: Mountainside traditional restaurant in Surrel, known for spit-roasted lamb and views over Tirana.
dest.cercizIsmetShehuTip: Go for lunch on a clear day to enjoy the terrace views over the hills above Tirana.
dest.odaDesc: Cosy Tirana restaurant serving traditional Albanian dishes in a rustic, folk-style setting.
dest.odaTip: The mixed meze platter is the easiest way to sample several regional specialties at once.
dest.mullixhiuDesc: Modern Albanian restaurant reviving old village recipes with a contemporary touch.
dest.mullixhiuTip: Save room for the dessert made with byrek pastry — a signature twist on a classic.

coverage.factTirana: Tirana’s Skanderbeg Square is one of the largest pedestrian squares in the Balkans.
coverage.factDurres: Durrës has one of the largest Roman amphitheatres in the Balkans.
coverage.factVlore: Albania’s independence was declared in Vlorë in 1912.
coverage.factSaranda: Sarandë enjoys around 300 sunny days a year.
coverage.factRiviera: The Llogara Pass drops from about 1,000 m almost straight down to the Riviera beaches.
coverage.factShkoder: Shkodër is one of the oldest cities in Europe, next to the largest lake in Southern Europe.
coverage.factBerat: Berat is known as the “town of a thousand windows”.
coverage.factAlps: The Theth–Valbona trail is Albania’s most famous alpine hike. Signal can be limited in deep valleys.
